ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Frances Burney Synthetic CCD — True-date frame: synthetic events are moved into the patient's historical lifetime. Codes, instruments, and treatments remain modern and are anachronistic.

text.paragraph: Primary care visit for a right breast lump and a year of breast ache. Concerns: A heavy, dull ache in the right breast for about a year and a firm lump she noticed two months ago; Dreads an operation; wants every step explained in advance and to be warned before anything is done. tr.td: Diagnostic bilateral mammography: 2.4 cm irregular spiculated mass at 10 o'clock in the upper outer right breast; heterogeneously dense breasts; left breast normal; BI-RADS 5
Right breast and axillary ultrasound: 2.5 cm irregular hypoechoic mass at 10 o'clock, 6 cm from the nipple; normal axillary lymph nodes
Ultrasound-guided core needle biopsy of the right breast mass with clip placement: invasive ductal carcinoma, grade 2; ER 95 percent, PR 70 percent, HER2 1+ (negative), Ki-67 15 percent

Bilateral breast MRI with contrast for extent of disease: index mass 2.6 cm; a second 0.8 cm enhancing mass at 7 o'clock in the right breast, 5 cm from the index mass; left breast normal; no enlarged nodes
MRI-guided core needle biopsy of the second right breast lesion: invasive ductal carcinoma, grade 2, ER positive, HER2 negative (multicentric disease)

Right total mastectomy without reconstruction, her choice, under general anesthesia; overnight stay. Pathology: multicentric invasive ductal carcinoma, 2.6 cm and 0.8 cm, grade 2, margins clear, no lymphovascular invasion; pT2(m) pN0(sn), anatomic stage IIA. Recurrence score (21-gene assay) 13
Right axillary sentinel lymph node biopsy at mastectomy (radioisotope and blue dye): 0 of 3 nodes involved
Ultrasound-guided pectoral nerve block (PECS II) with ropivacaine before incision, for pain control after mastectomy
Baseline bone density scan (DXA) before anastrozole: lumbar spine T-score -1.4, femoral neck T-score -1.7 (low bone mass)
Aspiration of a right chest wall seroma by the breast surgery team: 140 mL of clear straw-colored fluid; no signs of infection

code.displayName: Periodic reevaluation and management of healthy individual

tr.td: Diagnostic mammography and ultrasound, then image-guided core biopsy with ER, PR, and HER2 testing, for a palpable breast mass in a woman of 59
Breast surgery consultation to discuss surgical options, imaging of the extent of disease, axillary staging, and anesthesia and pain control
Germline genetic testing before surgery, as recommended for breast cancer diagnosed at 65 or younger
Right total mastectomy with sentinel lymph node biopsy under general anesthesia with a pectoral nerve block and an opioid-sparing recovery pathway

Anastrozole 1 mg daily for five years, with a baseline DXA repeated every two years, vitamin D and calcium, lipid monitoring, and questions about joint pain, hot flashes, and vaginal symptoms at every visit

Survivorship care: history and examination every 3 to 6 months for 3 years and a yearly mammogram of the left breast, with no routine blood tests or body imaging; lymphedema counseling and shoulder exercises; distress screening; a written survivorship care plan
Complete diagnosis, staging, and surgery within eight weeks of presentation
Core biopsy in four days, MRI and a second biopsy within four weeks, mastectomy at seven weeks
Surgery under anesthesia with pain controlled without opioids after discharge
Pain 2 out of 10 by the third day; no opioid after leaving hospital; acetaminophen stopped at two weeks
Start adjuvant endocrine therapy with a bone-health plan
Anastrozole started; baseline DXA shows low bone mass; vitamin D started
Regain full right shoulder movement and keep lymphedema risk low
Shoulder flexion 165 degrees at four weeks, nearly full, with physical therapy under way; arm circumferences equal

Three weeks after surgery: independent; right shoulder flexion 150 degrees and improving with exercises [S]
